namespace Pipeline.Generated

/-!
Model of POSIX `fold -w WIDTH` (WIDTH >= 1), plain character counting:
each input line is broken greedily into segments of at most WIDTH
characters; an empty input line stays one empty output line.
-/

/-- Greedy chunking of a character list: each emitted chunk is
`c :: cs.take k`, so every chunk is nonempty with length at most `k + 1`.
Called with `k = WIDTH - 1` so chunks have length at most WIDTH. -/
def chunksAux (k : Nat) : List Char → List (List Char)
  | [] => []
  | c :: cs => (c :: cs.take k) :: chunksAux k (cs.drop k)
  termination_by l => l.length
  decreasing_by simp only [List.length_drop, List.length_cons]; omega

/-- Chunks of one input line: an empty line yields one empty segment,
a nonempty line is chunked greedily. -/
def lineChunks (k : Nat) : List Char → List (List Char)
  | [] => [[]]
  | c :: cs => chunksAux k (c :: cs)

/-- Fold one input line into output segments of at most `w` characters
(for `w ≥ 1`); an empty line stays one empty line. -/
def foldLine (w : Nat) (s : String) : List String :=
  (lineChunks (w - 1) s.toList).map String.ofList

/-- Width from argv `["-w", N]`; the POSIX default is 80. Inputs outside
the modeled scope (missing/garbled/zero width, "results unspecified" per
POSIX) are clamped so the width is always positive. -/
def parseWidth (args : List String) : Nat :=
  match args with
  | ["-w", n] => max (n.toNat?.getD 80) 1
  | _ => 80

/-- `fold -w WIDTH` on stdin lines: fold each line independently,
exit status 0. -/
def run (args stdin : List String) : List String × UInt32 :=
  (stdin.flatMap (foldLine (parseWidth args)), 0)

/-! ## Helper lemmas -/

theorem chunksAux_flatten (k : Nat) (l : List Char) :
    (chunksAux k l).flatten = l := by
  fun_induction chunksAux k l with
  | case1 => rfl
  | case2 c cs ih => simp [ih, List.take_append_drop]

theorem chunksAux_mem_length (k : Nat) (l : List Char) :
    ∀ m ∈ chunksAux k l, m.length ≤ k + 1 := by
  fun_induction chunksAux k l with
  | case1 => intro m hm; simp at hm
  | case2 c cs ih =>
      intro m hm
      rcases List.mem_cons.mp hm with h | h
      · subst h
        simp only [List.length_cons, List.length_take]
        omega
      · exact ih m h

theorem chunksAux_of_short {k : Nat} {c : Char} {cs : List Char}
    (h : cs.length ≤ k) : chunksAux k (c :: cs) = [c :: cs] := by
  simp [chunksAux, List.take_of_length_le h, List.drop_of_length_le h]

theorem lineChunks_flatten (k : Nat) (l : List Char) :
    (lineChunks k l).flatten = l := by
  cases l with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons c cs => simp [lineChunks, chunksAux_flatten]

theorem lineChunks_ne_nil (k : Nat) (l : List Char) :
    lineChunks k l ≠ [] := by
  cases l with
  | nil => simp [lineChunks]
  | cons c cs => simp [lineChunks, chunksAux]

theorem lineChunks_mem_length (k : Nat) (l : List Char) :
    ∀ m ∈ lineChunks k l, m.length ≤ k + 1 := by
  cases l with
  | nil =>
      intro m hm
      simp only [lineChunks, List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hm
      simp [hm]
  | cons c cs => exact chunksAux_mem_length k (c :: cs)

theorem lineChunks_of_short {k : Nat} {l : List Char}
    (h : l.length ≤ k + 1) : lineChunks k l = [l] := by
  cases l with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons c cs =>
      simp only [List.length_cons] at h
      exact chunksAux_of_short (Nat.le_of_succ_le_succ h)

theorem foldLine_ne_nil (w : Nat) (s : String) : foldLine w s ≠ [] := by
  simp only [foldLine, ne_eq, List.map_eq_nil_iff]
  exact lineChunks_ne_nil (w - 1) s.toList

theorem foldLine_mem_length (w : Nat) (s t : String)
    (ht : t ∈ foldLine w s) : t.length ≤ w - 1 + 1 := by
  simp only [foldLine, List.mem_map] at ht
  obtain ⟨m, hm, rfl⟩ := ht
  simpa using lineChunks_mem_length (w - 1) s.toList m hm

theorem foldLine_toList_flatten (w : Nat) (s : String) :
    ((foldLine w s).map String.toList).flatten = s.toList := by
  simp [foldLine, List.map_map, Function.comp_def, lineChunks_flatten]

theorem foldLine_of_short {w : Nat} {s : String} (hw : 1 ≤ w)
    (hs : s.length ≤ w) : foldLine w s = [s] := by
  have h : s.toList.length ≤ (w - 1) + 1 := by
    rw [String.length_toList]; omega
  rw [foldLine, lineChunks_of_short h]
  simp

theorem parseWidth_pos (args : List String) : 1 ≤ parseWidth args := by
  unfold parseWidth
  split
  · exact Nat.le_max_right _ 1
  · omega

/-! ## Spec theorems -/

/-- EXIT STATUS: within the modeled scope all input is processed
successfully, so the exit status is always 0. -/
theorem run_exit_zero (args stdin : List String) :
    (run args stdin).2 = 0 := rfl

/-- Each input line is folded independently: the output for concatenated
input is the concatenation of the outputs (fold is a line filter and
STDOUT preserves input order). -/
theorem run_append (args xs ys : List String) :
    (run args (xs ++ ys)).1 = (run args xs).1 ++ (run args ys).1 := by
  simp [run]

/-- Every output segment has at most WIDTH characters: no output line
exceeds the width parsed from `-w`. -/
theorem run_width_bound (args stdin : List String) (line : String)
    (h : line ∈ (run args stdin).1) : line.length ≤ parseWidth args := by
  simp only [run, List.mem_flatMap] at h
  obtain ⟨s, _, hline⟩ := h
  have h1 := foldLine_mem_length (parseWidth args) s line hline
  have h2 := parseWidth_pos args
  omega

/-- STDOUT content preservation: the characters of the output, in order,
are exactly the characters of the input; fold only inserts line breaks. -/
theorem run_content_preserved (args stdin : List String) :
    ((run args stdin).1.map String.toList).flatten
      = (stdin.map String.toList).flatten := by
  induction stdin with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons s ss ih =>
      simp only [run, List.flatMap_cons, List.map_append, List.map_cons,
        List.flatten_append, List.flatten_cons] at *
      rw [foldLine_toList_flatten, ih]

/-- Every input line produces at least one output segment (an empty input
line stays one empty output line), so output has at least as many lines. -/
theorem run_line_count (args stdin : List String) :
    stdin.length ≤ (run args stdin).1.length := by
  induction stdin with
  | nil => exact Nat.le_refl 0
  | cons s ss ih =>
      simp only [run, List.flatMap_cons, List.length_append,
        List.length_cons] at *
      have h : (foldLine (parseWidth args) s).length ≠ 0 := by
        simpa [List.length_eq_zero_iff] using
          foldLine_ne_nil (parseWidth args) s
      omega

theorem flatMap_foldLine_self {w : Nat} (hw : 1 ≤ w) (out : List String)
    (h : ∀ l ∈ out, l.length ≤ w) : out.flatMap (foldLine w) = out := by
  induction out with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons l ls ih =>
      rw [List.flatMap_cons, foldLine_of_short hw (h l (by simp)),
        ih (fun x hx => h x (by simp [hx]))]
      rfl

/-- Idempotence: folding already-folded output changes nothing, since
every output segment already fits within the width. -/
theorem run_idempotent (args stdin : List String) :
    run args ((run args stdin).1) = run args stdin := by
  have hb : ∀ l ∈ (run args stdin).1, l.length ≤ parseWidth args :=
    fun l hl => run_width_bound args stdin l hl
  show ((run args stdin).1.flatMap (foldLine (parseWidth args)), 0)
      = run args stdin
  rw [flatMap_foldLine_self (parseWidth_pos args) _ hb]
  rfl

end Pipeline.Generated

spec_theorems.name: run_exit_zero
spec_theorems.informal: Within the modeled scope all input is processed successfully, so fold exits with status 0 for every argv and stdin.

spec_theorems.name: run_append
spec_theorems.informal: fold is a line filter: the output for concatenated input line lists is the concatenation of the per-part outputs, preserving input order.

spec_theorems.name: run_width_bound
spec_theorems.informal: Every output segment contains at most WIDTH characters, where WIDTH is the value parsed from -w.

spec_theorems.name: run_content_preserved
spec_theorems.informal: The characters of the output, in order, are exactly the characters of the input; fold only inserts line breaks and never adds, drops, or reorders characters.

spec_theorems.name: run_line_count
spec_theorems.informal: Every input line produces at least one output segment (an empty input line stays one empty output line), so the output has at least as many lines as the input.

spec_theorems.name: run_idempotent
spec_theorems.informal: Folding already-folded output at the same width changes nothing, since every segment already fits within WIDTH.
